domain_restrictions: k and l are between 0 and n inclusive
the Gaussian q-binomial coefficients are interpreted in their standard polynomial form
the quotient is assumed to be an actual polynomial in q, not merely a rational function
coefficients are understood as integer coefficients of a polynomial in q
root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every choice of integers n, k, l with 0 <= k <= n and 0 <= l <= n, if the quotient of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient [n choose k]_q by [n choose l]_q is itself a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has all coefficients nonnegative.
quantifier_order: For all integers n, k, l
assume 0 <= k and 0 <= l and k <= n and l <= n
if the quotient of the two Gaussian q-binomial coefficients is a polynomial in q
then every coefficient of that polynomial is nonnegative

variables.name: n
variables.role: index parameter for Gaussian binomial coefficients

variables.name: k
variables.role: lower index of the first Gaussian binomial coefficient

variables.name: l
variables.role: lower index of the second Gaussian binomial coefficient

variables.name: q
variables.role: variable in which the quotient is assumed to be a polynomial

payload.theorem_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.
